briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion-2 and Google Gemini-3 push multi-agent frontiers as compute shortages intensify

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has accelerated into 2026 with frontier labs releasing iterative model upgrades weekly. Funding remains robust despite regulatory headwinds, while safety concerns center on production deployments. DialectForge emerges as a protocol-level solution amid rising injection risks.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed Orion-2 with enhanced agentic capabilities, while Anthropic's Claude 4.1 and Meta's Llama-4-405B compete on coding benchmarks. DeepSeek-V4 and xAI's Grok-3 show strong gains in multilingual reasoning.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and IoT environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp reaches 2M units monthly as Microsoft and Google expand 100k+ GPU clusters. TSMC reports record AI chip demand through Q3 2026.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will protocol-level defenses like dynamic dialects become mandatory for all frontier multi-agent deployments by 2027?
